text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- After having consultations with parties, Andris Shkele proposed his model of the next government, which gives three ministries to each of the major factions and four to the bloc of small ones.

- The Democratic Party Saimnieks will get the ministries of finance, interior and education, Fatherland & Freedom the economics, justice and welfare posts while Latvia's Way will receive the transport, foreign, environment protection and regional development ministries while the bloc of small factions will receive defence, culture, agriculture and European Affairs.

- A delegation of Russian foreign ministry experts met with the assistant state secretary of the Latvian Foreign Ministry, Aivis Ronis. They have agreed on starting the work of the intergovernmental commission, resuming talks on the border issue, as well as consultations between the two foreign ministries.
- A Foreign Ministery spokesman said no Latvian officials will attend the inauguration of Chechen president Aslan Maskhadov.
- The cabinet accepted the draft law on the prevention of money laundering.
- The staff of the state-run transportation company in the central Cesis district went on one-day strike to protest against misuse of funds by the management and laying off bus drivers.

- The cabinet accepted rules which provide that all deals in cash totalling more than 1,000 lats per month must be disclosed in special cash deals declarations and submitted to the state revenue service.
- Latvian food processing plants have got certificates to export their produce to Lithuania and Estonia.
